topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, learning objectives, and central questions regarding the origin and causes of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: endogenous mutations, genetics, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad conceptual frameworks of cancer development, comparing intrinsic replicative errors with inherited genetics and environmental risks demonstrated by epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Pathogens and viral mechanisms in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, illustrated in detail by the mechanism and epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental chemicals and radiation undergo metabolic processing to form reactive intermediates that cause direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promoters, inflammation, and multi-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics contrast non-mutagenic tumor promoters that stimulate proliferation and chronic inflammation with mutagenic initiators in the multi-stage model of cancer.

topics.label: Host developmental susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how tissue context and life stage determine vulnerability to carcinogens, followed by a summary of the direct and indirect mechanisms of DNA damage.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine mutagenic signatures and test chemical carcinogenicity.
